title: Words Teachers Use
objectives: I can tell what ten words mean when teachers use them in directions.
I can follow a direction like select, rank, or outline.
I can use the words to tell the steps of writing a report.
I can show I understand a direction by doing it.
rationale: Students show what they know in every subject by following task words: identify, locate, recall, select, revise, combine, gather, outline, edit, and rank. Many third graders can do the task but miss the word, so a misread direction looks like a gap in knowledge. These ten words are the ones most common in grade 3 science, social studies, and writing directions. The unit follows weather and social studies on purpose, so the verbs can be practiced on content students already know. Revise and edit are taught as a pair, because students often treat them as the same step.

words.def: To find out and say what something is.
words.ex: Can you identify the bird by its song?
words.ex2: Students identify the main character in each story.
words.nonExample: Guessing a bird's name without looking is not a way to identify it.

apps.academic: In science, we identify rocks by their color and how they feel.
apps.spoken: I can identify my backpack by its patch.
apps.writing: Use identify when a direction asks you to name what something is.

cloze.s: The scientist used a field guide to ___ the strange leaf she found on the trail.

cloze2.s: Please ___ the main idea of the paragraph and write it on the line below.

misuse.s: She was asked to identify the bird, so she wrote her name at the top and sat down.
misuse.why: To identify is to say what something is; she did not name the bird.

visual.alt: A magnifying glass over a small bird.

words.frame: I can identify a ___ by its ___.

words.ex2: Dana used a flashlight to locate her lost mitten under the couch.
words.nonExample: Closing a map and putting it away does not help you locate a place.

apps.academic: In social studies, we locate a country on a map or a globe.
apps.spoken: I cannot locate my left shoe.
apps.writing: Use locate when a direction asks you to find a place or an object.

cloze.s: Use the map key to ___ the library, which is shown with a small book symbol.

cloze2.s: The ship's crew used a compass and chart to ___ the island before the sun set.

misuse.s: Please locate the town on the map by throwing the map into the trash.
misuse.why: To locate is to find where something is; throwing the map away does not do that.

visual.alt: A map with a pin on it.

words.frame: To locate ___ on a map, I look for ___.

words.def: To remember something and bring it back to mind.
words.ex: Can you recall the three steps of the water cycle?
words.ex2: I recall the smell of fresh bread in Grandma's kitchen.
words.nonExample: Forgetting a fact is the opposite of recalling it.

apps.academic: In science, a quiz may ask you to recall facts you learned last week.
apps.spoken: Do you recall where we put the glue?
apps.writing: Use recall when a direction asks you to remember something you learned.

cloze.s: When the teacher asked about last week's story, Omar could ___ every character's name.

cloze2.s: Try to ___ what you read yesterday before you start the new chapter.

misuse.s: I recall the story by never having heard it once in my whole life.
misuse.why: To recall is to remember something from before; she never heard the story.

visual.alt: A thought bubble beside a brain.

words.def: To choose one or more things from a group.
words.ex: Select the best title for the story.
words.ex2: Each player will select one card from the pile.
words.nonExample: Taking everything from the shelf is not selecting.

apps.academic: On a test, select the answer that best fits the question.
apps.spoken: Please select a book from the cart.
apps.writing: Use select when a direction asks you to choose from a group.

cloze.s: From the three paintings, the judges will ___ the one with the brightest colors as the winner.

cloze2.s: Each student may ___ one book from the cart to take home for the weekend.

misuse.s: She selected a card by leaving every card on the table and choosing none of them.
misuse.why: Select means to choose one; choosing none does not fit.

visual.alt: A check mark beside a stack of books.

words.def: To change your writing to make it better.
words.ex: After the first draft, she will revise her opening sentence.
words.ex2: Revise your paragraph by adding more details.
words.nonExample: Leaving every word exactly the same is not revising.

apps.academic: In writing, we revise to make the ideas clearer and stronger.
apps.spoken: I need to revise my story's ending.
apps.writing: Use revise when a direction asks you to improve your ideas or words.

cloze.s: Mia read her draft aloud and decided to ___ the middle by adding a few vivid details.

cloze2.s: The editor asked the author to ___ the ending, because the story felt too short.

misuse.s: Revise your story by leaving every word exactly the same and handing it in.
misuse.why: To revise is to change writing to make it better, not to leave it the same.

visual.alt: A pencil and a page of writing.

words.frame: To revise my writing, I can ___.

words.def: To join two or more things into one.
words.ex: Combine the flour and sugar in a large bowl.
words.ex2: Combine two short sentences to make one long one.
words.nonExample: Keeping two things in separate bowls is not combining them.

apps.academic: In math, we combine two groups to find how many in all.
apps.spoken: Combine the paint colors to make green.
apps.writing: Use combine when a direction asks you to join things together.

cloze.s: To make orange paint, ___ red and yellow in the same cup and stir them together.

cloze2.s: Please ___ the two short sentences into one longer sentence with the word and.

misuse.s: Combine the milk and eggs by keeping them in separate bowls at opposite ends of the room.
misuse.why: To combine is to join together; separate bowls do the opposite.

visual.alt: A mixing bowl and a paint palette.

words.frame: I can combine ___ and ___ to make ___.

words.def: To bring things or people together in one place.
words.ex: Please gather your books and line up at the door.
words.ex2: Birds gather on the wire at sunset.
words.nonExample: Scattering papers across the floor is the opposite of gathering them.

apps.academic: In science, we gather data by counting and measuring.
apps.spoken: Let's gather around the table to see the map.
apps.writing: Use gather when a direction asks you to collect facts or things.

cloze.s: Before writing a report, you should ___ facts from books, charts, and talking to an expert.

cloze2.s: At the sound of the bell, the whole class will ___ on the rug for the story.

misuse.s: The class will gather by running to the four corners of the field and staying far apart.
misuse.why: Gather means to bring together; staying far apart does the opposite.

visual.alt: A basket and a group of people.

words.def: To plan a piece of writing by listing its main parts.
words.ex: Outline your story before you start writing it.
words.ex2: Mr. Lee asked us to outline the chapter in three steps.
words.nonExample: Writing the whole story with no plan first is not outlining.

apps.academic: In writing, we outline our ideas with a heading for each main part.
apps.spoken: I will outline my report before I write it.
apps.writing: Use outline when a direction asks you to list main parts in order.

cloze.s: To ___ his report on bats, Sam wrote one heading for food, one for homes, and one for sleep.

cloze2.s: Before the big test, Dee will ___ the chapter by listing each main idea and a key detail.

misuse.s: Outline your report by writing the whole thing in one long paragraph with no plan.
misuse.why: To outline is to list the main parts first, not to write the finished report.

visual.alt: A clipboard list and a hand writing.

words.frame: To outline my ___, I will list ___.

words.ex: Edit your story for spelling and capital letters.
words.ex2: Maya will edit her report with a green pen.
words.nonExample: Adding more mistakes on purpose is the opposite of editing.

apps.academic: In writing, we edit last, after we revise, to fix spelling and punctuation.
apps.spoken: Please edit your name at the top of the page.
apps.writing: Use edit when a direction asks you to fix mistakes.

cloze.s: After you finish your story, ___ it for spelling mistakes and missing periods.

cloze2.s: The class will ___ each other's papers with a green pen, circling any misspelled words.

misuse.s: Edit your story by adding more spelling mistakes on purpose.
misuse.why: Edit means to fix mistakes, not to add more.

visual.alt: A pen and a check mark.

words.frame: When I edit, I check for ___.

words.def: To put things in order from first to last.
words.ex: Rank the planets by size from smallest to largest.
words.ex2: The judges will rank the three best science projects.
words.nonExample: Mixing the cards up so there is no order is not ranking them.

apps.academic: In social studies, we rank the reasons from most to least important.
apps.writing: Use rank when a direction asks you to put things in order.

cloze.s: The coach will ___ the runners from fastest to slowest, with a number for each.

cloze2.s: Please ___ the three facts from most important to least important and number them one, two, and three.

misuse.s: Rank the puppies by mixing them up so that there is no order at all.
misuse.why: To rank is to put things in order, not to mix them up.

visual.alt: A gold medal and a silver medal.

passage.title: Priya's Weather Report
paras: Mr. Shah's class had a big job: write a report about the weather in their town. First, the students had to gather information. They read books, studied charts, and asked a weather expert to visit.

Next, Priya had to identify the main parts of the climate where she lived. She used a map to locate the nearest weather station. Then she tried to recall what the class had learned about the forecast and how puddles evaporate into the air.

With many facts in her notes, Priya had to select the three that mattered most. She chose rainfall, temperature, and wind, and she tried to rank them from most to least important. She wrote an outline with a heading for each part. Then she began to write, and she was able to combine two short sentences into one smooth sentence.

After her first draft, Priya was ready to revise. She added a stronger opening and took out a repeated idea. Last, she would edit for spelling and capital letters. On Friday, she read her report to the class, and her friends clapped.

qs.q: In paragraph 4, the word "revise" most nearly means
qs.why: Priya adds a stronger opening and takes out a repeated idea, so revise means to change writing to make it better.

qs.q: Why did Priya select only three facts?
choices: The three facts were the most important ones for her report.
She did not have any other facts.
Her teacher told her to stop reading.
qs.why: The text says she picked the three that mattered most.

qs.q: Which detail shows that Priya planned before she wrote?
choices: She asked a weather expert to visit.
She read her report on Friday.
She wrote an outline with a heading for each part.
qs.why: An outline is a plan, and the text says she made one before she began to write.

qs.q: What is this passage mostly about?
choices: The steps Priya followed to research and write a weather report
Friends who clap for each other
qs.why: The passage lists the steps from gathering facts to revising and editing.

teacher.overview: Students learn ten common task words from classroom directions, read a story about a student who researches and writes a weather report, and practice following each direction.

notes.va.identify.v: Identify means to name what something is. Have students identify objects from a bag by touch, then say how they knew.
notes.va.locate.v: Locate means to find where. Practice with a map or the classroom: Locate the pencil sharpener.
notes.va.recall.v: Recall is to remember from before. Ask: what did we learn yesterday? Link to the forecast and climate words from the weather unit.
notes.va.select.v: Select is choose, usually on a test. Give three options and ask students to select one and explain why.
notes.va.revise.v: Revise is about ideas and details, like adding or moving. Edit is about spelling and punctuation. Students mix them up, so teach them as a pair.
notes.va.combine.v: Combine joins two things. Use paint and sentence examples. Contrast with separate.
notes.va.gather.v: Gather means to bring together. In research, it means to collect facts. Ask students where they can gather facts.
notes.va.outline.v: Outline here is a verb: to plan by listing main parts. Students may know it as a noun for the shape around a drawing; mention both.
notes.va.edit.v: Edit is to fix mistakes. Give a sentence with errors and have students edit it with a colored pen.
notes.va.rank.v: Rank is to put in order. Give three items and ask students to rank them and justify the order.

teacher.model: Think-aloud: "The direction says rank the facts. Rank means to put them in order. I will decide which fact matters most, write a 1 next to it, then a 2 and a 3. I did what the word asked, so I can check my work."

Recall means to look something up.
Outline only means a line drawn around a picture.
